summary.headline: S H Kelkar H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 14% to Rs.1,299 crore and EBITDA 33% to Rs.168 crore, with margin at 13%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations grew 15% YoY to Rs.636 crore, and H1 revenue reached Rs.1,299 crore (up 14%). H1 EBITDA rose 33% to Rs.168 crore, margin about 13%, with gross margins broadly stable despite raw material volatility. Flavour revenue grew 47% in H1 to Rs.184 crore, though management called part of Q1 a one-off inventory build by customers. Net debt stood at Rs.911 crore at September 30, 2026, which management expects to be the peak for the year as inventory is reduced.

segments.name: Fragrance
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.1,088 crore, up 11.9% YoY; management cites about 14% underlying growth excluding roughly Rs.50 crore of low-margin business hived off in Q4 FY26. Domestic growth about 9% (roughly 5% price, 4% volume).

segments.name: Flavour
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.184 crore, up 47% YoY; Q2 revenue about Rs.72 crore versus a Q1 that was higher. Management sees Rs.90 crore per quarter as the run rate and about 20% sustainable growth.

segments.name: Overseas CDCs (Germany, UK, US)
segments.commentary: First sales achieved in all three markets; revenue is small and management says it will take 12-18 months to become meaningful. Around Rs.80 crore of spend in these centres is not yet generating meaningful revenue.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 12-13% per year on a continuing basis over the next 2-3 years, with EBITDA growth of 13-14% per year.
Gross margin expected in the 43% range; upside of about 0.5% if raw material and geopolitical conditions ease.
EBITDA margin of 15%+ targeted within 12-18 months at steady-state inflation, or about two years if inflation persists; 13% described as the lower end of sustainable.
Interest cost expected at Rs.16-17 crore per quarter in H2 FY27; D&A expected at Rs.145-150 crore annualised after new facility capitalisation.
Net debt expected to fall from September 2026 peak by March 2027; insurance claim settlement expected by March 2027.
Remaining FY27 capex about Rs.30-35 crore; FY28 capex about Rs.75-80 crore including spillover, with maintenance capex about Rs.15 crore.
capex_capacity: Europe capex almost complete; Europe factory operational since May 2026 and fully operational in Q2.
India Fragrance factory renewal expected to be completed and put to use in Q4 FY27; transition from Mulund follows in FY28.
Second factory (Vanavate or Vashivali) expected to be put to use in Q4 FY28, concluding the large expansion.
Jakarta (Southeast Asia) factory in full operation since September 2025, improving lead times to clients.
Overseas development centres in Germany, Manchester (UK) and US are fully staffed and in use; no further CDC investment planned.
demand_pricing: Domestic Fragrance growth split roughly 5% price and 4% volume; large clients are growing faster than smaller clients, which management calls transient.
Excluding about Rs.25 crore of intentionally exited low-margin categories, like-for-like growth is about 12%.
Management expects a stabilisation in raw material prices and strong H2 demand, but flagged the Middle East situation as the biggest risk.
Flavour growth in Q1 was partly a one-off as customers built inventory due to freight and logistics disruption; management expects about 20% sustainable growth.
More than 5,000 clients served globally; no specific RFQs cited. Europe and US smaller-brand and mid-size opportunities are being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fragrance growth split between volume and value in domestic market?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 5% from price and 4% from volume in the domestic Fragrance business, which grew about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: When will inventory unwind and working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory reduction started in October 2026; management does not expect a sharp total inventory fall but expects lower inventory intensity as sales grow over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable interest and depreciation run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest about Rs.16-17 crore per quarter in H2 FY27; D&A about Rs.145-150 crore annualised, with European acquisition amortisation reducing from 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Flavour Q2 run rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 at about Rs.72 crore was below the normal run rate and Rs.90 crore per quarter is the right run rate; Q1 was above it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROCE below 12% since 2019?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mature India businesses earn about 20% ROCE; overseas investment, the 2024 expansion and fire-related domestic capex weigh on the figure. Rs.80 crore of CDC spend is not yet earning returns.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone margin low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operations moved to subsidiaries KFG and KFL after the fire, so standalone margins are not representative and should recover once operations move back next year.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict, raw material inflation and availability, and geopolitical outcomes after the US midterm elections.
Net debt of Rs.911 crore at September 2026 and working capital tied up in high inventory; delivery on the March 2027 reduction target.
Flavour growth lumpiness from customer order timing and inventory destocking after Q1 one-off demand.
Overseas CDCs take 12-18 months to become meaningful; ROCE remains below 12% in the near term.
Execution of Fragrance factory renewal (Q4 FY27) and second factory (Q4 FY28) with capex spillover into FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and margin recovery, but cautious on near-term inflation and geopolitics; management repeatedly declined to extrapolate the 40%+ Flavour growth and reset the base to about 20%.
key_quotes: We expect September debt level to represent a peak for the year with the reduction anticipated by March 2027 as we optimize inventory levels.
So, we expect 14% on a 12% revenue growth, 13% to 14% EBITDA growth year-on-year in the next 2-3 years.

It will take a good three to four years before we are breakeven in those markets by themselves and then another further three to four years as we continue to grow to generate meaningful returns on this investment.

growth.why: Management guides 12-13% continuing revenue growth and 15%+ EBITDA margin in 12-18 months, backed by Europe factory (live), India factory renewal (Q4 FY27) and second factory (Q4 FY28), but no firm order book or RFQs cited, so backing is partial.
